result.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds
result.summary: Video games provide a practical setting for collecting vision-language-action (VLA) data, whose acquisition in physical environments is costly. Existing datasets, however, remain limited by restricted game coverage, sparse language supervision, or temporal hierarchies that do not necessarily reflect changes in task objectives. We introduce AceAction, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games for learning skill composition and subgoal transitions. AceAction organizes demonstrations around complete tasks, linking overall instructions, ordered subgoals, and local skill instructions to temporally aligned visual observations and keyboard-and-mouse actions. To construct these annotations, we develop a vision-language model pipeline that identifies subgoals from changes in objectives or interaction targets, anchors navigation goals to visually recognizable waypoints, and composes adjacent subgoals into task instructions. The resulting demonstrations cover navigation, reconnaissance, combat, interaction, and recovery, with explicit stage boundaries that connect task progression to fine-grained control. We assess annotation quality through model-based verification and human inspection. An audit of 500 trajectories yields a 95.8% pass rate across independent reviewer assessments. AceAction provides a data foundation for studying how agents execute, combine, and switch skills to follow complex instructions in dynamic game environments.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建跨多个 3D 游戏的人类游玩 VLA 数据集 AceAction，将整体任务指令、有序子目标与局部技能指令同视觉观测和键鼠动作对齐，并用 VLM 流水线依据目标或交互对象变化切分子目标、锚定导航路点。
AI.relevance_reason: 其显式阶段边界与子目标切换标注可作为轨迹级监督结构的线索，供核查能否用于 latent 推理中的子目标状态更新、切换与停止信号建模；但论文本身面向游戏 VLA 数据，未涉及 latent 表示。
